newsitem.title: UK: Spain's GDP growth will permit lower deficit-Rato.
newsitem.headline: Spain's GDP growth will permit lower deficit-Rato.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Monday the country would be able to continue reducing its public deficit because GDP was growing more quickly than inflation.

"The big change to the Spanish economy is that output is growing faster than prices, and that is giving the economy a very good chance of combining an investment policy in the public sector with a reduction of the public deficit," Rato, in London for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development meeting, told Reuters.
A three-year fiscal discipline plan was approved by the Spanish government on Friday.
It aims to reduce Spain's public deficit to 1.6 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2000 from a projected 3.0 percent in 1997. Average growth is seen at 3.2 percent through the year 2000.
Rato said to reduce the deficit the government would also have to work within a tight budget and planned to introduce more competition to the production to public goods.
In an earlier interview, Rato said he did not see Spanish inflation picking up in the second half of the year and Spain would stick with its 2.6 percent official target for inflation.
